image_description: A black wrought-iron bannister system installed on an outdoor staircase. The railing features a continuous top handrail with decorative scrollwork at the corners and ends, supported by vertical balusters that include both straight bars and ornamental curved elements. The structure follows the diagonal incline of the stairs and includes a thicker newel post at the corner turn. The background shows white stucco walls and a glimpse of a roof or upper landing.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Vertical railing system following staircase geometry creating diagonal linear pattern.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The railing clearly follows the diagonal slope of the stairs in the foreground and the horizontal/vertical geometry of the landing in the background.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Continuous handrail supported by evenly spaced balusters.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A continuous black metal rail runs along the top, supported by vertical elements. Spacing appears consistent within each section.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Balusters are slender cylindrical or turned posts of narrow diameter, closely spaced relative to their height.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vertical supports are slender metal bars, consistent with the 'slender' description, though they are flat/rectangular rather than cylindrical, which is acceptable for metalwork.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Handrail is smooth rounded or molded strip running parallel to staircase incline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The top rail appears smooth and follows the incline of the stairs accurately.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Newel posts thicker vertical supports anchor ends and corners.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is a distinct, thicker vertical post at the corner where the railing turns, acting as an anchor/newel post.
The railing geometry matches the underlying stair structure perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Materials range from polished wood with ornate turnings to sleek metal with minimal design.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The material is clearly black metal (wrought iron style) with ornate scroll designs, fitting the taxonomy description.
Visual texture and thinness confirm metal construction.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Evenly spaced vertical posts creating rhythmic pattern.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vertical bars create a consistent rhythmic visual pattern along the length of the railing.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The horizontal lines of the background wall and the roof edge show slight waviness and non-linear perspective convergence, suggesting minor geometric instability common in AI generations.
The surface of the stairs lacks distinct texture detail (e.g., concrete grain or stone veins), appearing as a smooth, slightly noisy gray gradient rather than a physical material.
Some connections between the vertical balusters and the bottom rail appear slightly fused or indistinct, lacking clear mechanical joints or welds.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the object is correctly classified as a bannister/balustrade and not a generic fence or gate.
To verify the 3D structural integrity of the railing relative to the stairs and check for floating elements or depth bleeding.
To ensure the thin metal bars are continuous and not broken or fused into the background, checking for edge artifacts.
To assess the realism of the metal textures and lighting consistency.

focus_areas: Continuity of the handrail around the corner newel post
Structural plausibility of the thin metal balusters
Geometric alignment of the railing with the stair incline
Texture realism of the metal and stair surfaces
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the connection points of the wrought iron. AI often struggles with the complex intersections of scrollwork and straight bars. Verify if the 'newel post' is structurally sound or just a thickened bar. Check if the background perspective lines are straight, as warping here indicates generative instability.
